title: Where no family can go
hookLine: where no mother, father, child or friend can go, the Name goes with you (Sukhmani 2)
tomorrow: The Name on the hard road

lines: THIS IS AS FAR AS YOU GO.
cards: A hospital corridor, late. A family has walked with someone as far as they can: the parking lot, the waiting room, the double doors marked staff only. Then a nurse gently says, this is as far as you go.

The doors swing shut, and everyone who loves the patient is on the wrong side. There are places a person has to go without the people who love them. The second ashtpadi's first stanza walks right up to that door.

teach.h: NO MOTHER, FATHER, CHILD OR FRIEND.
teach.b: The stanza begins, in paraphrase: where there is no mother, no father, no children, no friends, no brother, there, O mind, the Name goes with you as your help.
The opening words are jah maat pitaa sut meet na bhaaee: a person's closest ties, named one by one, and set down at the door. Then the stanza goes into harder places still.

teach.h: THE NAME GOES WITH YOU AS HELP.
teach.b: In paraphrase: where the great and terrible messenger of death would crush you, there only the Name goes along with you. Where the difficulty is very heavy, the Name of God saves you in an instant.
Notice what the stanza isn't saying. It isn't saying your family doesn't matter, or that love is useless. Sikh teaching honors the householder's life, the life of family and work.
The stanza points at something plainer: there are rooms other people can't enter with you. The operating room. The last hours of a life.
And, in the stanza's own picture, the meeting with the messenger of death.
In every one of those rooms, it says, there is a companion who doesn't stop at the door. Read at a bedside, the stanza doesn't say the family isn't enough.
It says the family can't go everywhere, and in the stanza's words, the Name can.

how: Some Sikh families read this stanza, or the whole of Sukhmani, at the bedside of someone who is ill or dying.

o: a title of honor given to a teacher
the family name handed down to children
the Name: God remembered, who goes with you

games.q: the first stanza of ashtpadi 2 — tap the pairs.
p: goes with you as your help

s: the stanza says family doesn't matter
it says there are places family can't follow, and the Name goes there too.
Sikh teaching honors the householder's life
the life of family and work; the stanza never says family doesn't matter.
the stanza says the Name saves in an instant where the difficulty is heavy
where the difficulty is very heavy, the Name saves you in an instant.

games.q: you've walked someone you love as far as the doors marked staff only. what does the stanza say goes on with them?
o: the Name of God, as their help.
games.why: where no mother, father, child or friend can go, there, O mind, the Name goes with you as your help.

practice: Picture the people who walk with you as far as they can, and be grateful for each one; then picture a door they can't come through, and you stepping through it.
If you pray, say Waheguru and imagine the Name stepping through beside you; if you don't, notice your own breath, which also comes with you everywhere.

wordCard.voice: Naam, the Name: the first stanza of Sukhmani's second ashtpadi, where no mother, father, child or friend can follow, the Name goes with you as your help.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: naam, the Name; in the stanza, the companion who goes where no family can.

carryVoice: Your line: the name goes too. Love walks you all the way to the door. Four hundred forty-three days now.

sources.ref: Gauri Sukhmani M5, ashtpadi 2, pauri 1, Ang 264
